Select and compute columns

Source: R/select_or_transmute.R
select_or_transmute.Rd

An enhanced dplyr::select() that also accepts data-masking expressions. As with dplyr::transmute(), only the selected and computed columns are returned.

Usage

select_or_transmute(.data, ...)

Arguments

.data

A data frame or tibble.

...

<tidy-select> selections or <data-masking> expressions. Omit to return the input unchanged.

Value

A table containing the selected and computed columns in argument order. Data-frame classes and grouping follow dplyr::select(); a tibble input returns a tibble. Grouping columns are retained. Unnamed computed columns use their expression as the name.

Details

Each argument is classified before evaluation. Column names, strings, numeric positions, selection syntax (c(), :, !, &, |, unary -) and tidyselect helpers such as starts_with(), where(), all_of() or varlist() select existing columns, as do calls that use no column names (for example all_of(vars) or seq_len(2)). Any other expression that uses columns, such as lexp >= 70 or gnp_thousands = gnppc / 1000, is computed with dplyr::mutate() and then selected, so arithmetic is never misread as column positions. Selections and computed values can be mixed; output follows argument order.

A named constant such as one = 1, label = "x" or y = c(1, 2) creates a constant column; it never selects or renames columns by position. Unnamed names, strings and positions must identify existing columns. If they do not, an error lists every unmatched name instead of evaluating them as expressions, so a misspelled column is never replaced by an object of the same name in the calling environment. (A symbol naming a character vector in the calling environment is still passed to tidyselect, which deprecates that form in favour of all_of().)

If selection itself fails for another reason (for example, duplicate output names), the arguments are evaluated sequentially with dplyr::transmute(); if that also fails, the error reports both attempts. Computed expressions are evaluated once when selection succeeds. Grouping columns are retained according to dplyr's selection rules.

See also

Other selection and preview functions: special-print, varlist()

Examples

lifeexp |>
  select_or_transmute()
#> # A tibble: 68 x 6
#>    region               country                popgrowth  lexp gnppc safewater
#>    <dbl+lbl>            <chr>                      <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>     <dbl>
#>  1 1 [Europe & C. Asia] Albania                     -0.6    74   870        49
#>  2 1 [Europe & C. Asia] Armenia                     -1.2    70   570        83
#>  3 1 [Europe & C. Asia] Austria                      0.1    78 27810        97
#>  4 1 [Europe & C. Asia] Azerbaijan                   0.9    64   510        49
#>  5 1 [Europe & C. Asia] Belarus                     -0.5    68  1540        82
#>  6 1 [Europe & C. Asia] Belgium                      0.2    77 26530       100
#>  7 1 [Europe & C. Asia] Bosnia and Herzegovina       1.8    74  1230        87
#>  8 1 [Europe & C. Asia] Bulgaria                    -0.7    71  1440        90
#>  9 1 [Europe & C. Asia] Croatia                     -0.1    72    NA        85
#> 10 1 [Europe & C. Asia] Czechia                     -0.1    75  6140        95
#> # i 58 more rows

lifeexp |>
  select_or_transmute(country, lexp)
#> # A tibble: 68 x 2
#>    country                 lexp
#>    <chr>                  <dbl>
#>  1 Albania                   74
#>  2 Armenia                   70
#>  3 Austria                   78
#>  4 Azerbaijan                64
#>  5 Belarus                   68
#>  6 Belgium                   77
#>  7 Bosnia and Herzegovina    74
#>  8 Bulgaria                  71
#>  9 Croatia                   72
#> 10 Czechia                   75
#> # i 58 more rows

# Ordinary select() rejects this computed expression.
try(dplyr::select(lifeexp, lexp >= 70))
#> Error in dplyr::select(lifeexp, lexp >= 70) : 
#>   i In argument: `lexp >= 70`.
#> Caused by error:
#> ! object 'lexp' not found

lifeexp |>
  select_or_transmute(lexp >= 70)
#> # A tibble: 68 x 1
#>    `lexp >= 70`
#>    <lgl>       
#>  1 TRUE        
#>  2 TRUE        
#>  3 TRUE        
#>  4 FALSE       
#>  5 FALSE       
#>  6 TRUE        
#>  7 TRUE        
#>  8 TRUE        
#>  9 TRUE        
#> 10 TRUE        
#> # i 58 more rows
